$comment: dsh-timer state file format contract. The plugin is the sole writer of these files; they are read-only for operators. The structural keywords below hold for the shape the plugin writes; on load the plugin runs a full-shape validation, and unknown extra keys (such as the legacy `missed` field and the legacy per-condition `lastTriggerMs`) are tolerated and never written back, and run records evicted from the FIFO before settlement may omit optional fields.
title: dsh-timer state file
description: Runtime state of one scheduled job. Each job has one state file named <jobId>.json under the state subdirectory of the plugin jobsDir (the state directory is excluded from the directory watch). The in-memory state is authoritative and the file is a best-effort mirror: a failed write does not block scheduling, and a missing file means the job has no persisted state yet. The plugin creates the file when the job is first loaded.

schemaVersion.description: State file schema version. A file whose version does not equal the current one is treated as corrupt: an enabled job is reset to a fresh state, a disabled job keeps its in-memory state.

jobId.description: Job id. It equals the name of this state file without the .json extension, and the name of the job file under the jobsDir.

lastActivationMs.description: Epoch milliseconds of the start moment of the most recent run (the activation base of onActiveSec). Null when the job has no run history in its state.

lastTriggerMs.description: Epoch milliseconds of the job's last on-calendar elapse moment (a fired trigger, or a due trigger consumed in place by an overlap=skip — the recompute anchor, one shared moment for all of the job's calendar conditions). Null when no on-calendar elapse has been persisted yet; absent in files written by older versions (tolerated on load, treated as no anchor). Never advanced by monotonic or manual fires.

value.description: The calendar condition value (a cron expression or an ISO datetime), identical to the key of this entry.

neverMatch.description: True when the cron expression is accepted but never matches a time; such a condition is reported as having no future match.

consumed.description: True when a one-shot (ISO datetime) condition has already fired in the persisted state; the condition then never fires again.

nextFireMs.description: Epoch milliseconds of the next trigger moment of this condition, or null when the condition has no future match (consumed one-shot or never-matching cron).

calendars.description: Per-condition state of the job's calendar conditions, keyed by the condition value exactly as written in the job file. Monotonic conditions (onActiveSec, onStartupSec) are not persisted: they are derived from lastActivationMs and the process start moment.

runId.description: Unique id of this run; the status output shows the full id, and the run verb report shows its first eight characters.

sessionId.description: Session id of the run session; the session transcript is the permanent audit trail of the run.

trigger.description: What started the run: one of scheduled, monotonic, startup, manual.

startedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds when the run started.

finishedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds when the run settled. Null while the run is in progress.

durationMs.description: Run duration in milliseconds. Null while the run is in progress.

status.description: running while the run is in progress; finished or failed after it settles. A record that was still running when the process ended is backfilled as failed with cause interrupted on the next start.

cause.description: Failure reason when the status is failed: timeout (the run exceeded runtimeMaxSec), cancelled, interrupted (process restart or stop), turn_error, or create_failed (the run session could not be created). Null for a finished run.

summary.description: Result summary of the run, truncated to 2000 characters; an empty string when the session produced no summary. Null while the run is in progress.

error.description: Error detail of a failed run, such as the interruption note on a process restart.

runs.description: Run audit records, oldest first. The writer keeps at most 50 entries (FIFO). A record that started but has not settled yet carries explicit nulls for cause, finishedAt, durationMs, and summary; a record evicted by the FIFO before settlement is re-appended at settlement with the fields that are known.

runs.summary: One-sentence heartbeat with the current time
